subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` stay on the owner-scoped private SSRF runtime surface, or may it be promoted through the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` subpath to fix the package lazy-load regression?
rationale: The PR assumes the public subpath is the right long-term target, but current source comments, guardrails, and sibling reviews keep the managed-proxy bypass helper private unless maintainers deliberately approve a new SDK/security contract.

options.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Access
options.body: Fix packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam, without adding this bypass helper to the public SDK.

options.title: Approve Public SDK Promotion
options.body: Promote the helper only with explicit SDK/security approval, aligned docs, contract checks, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Pick A Canonical Replacement
options.body: Pause or close competing branches once maintainers choose one sibling PR or replacement branch as the canonical repair for the same regression.

recommendation.title: Preserve Private Owner-Scoped Access
recommendation.body: Fix packaged Browser/Ollama resolution through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam, without adding this bypass helper to the public SDK.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is primarily SDK/package boundary direction, and history links this person to adjacent package-boundary and browser ownership work.
